itens.resumo: Cardinal who administers the temporal goods and ordinary affairs of the Holy See during the Sede Vacante, without holding power of governance over the universal Church, a prerogative of the College of Cardinals and, afterward, of the new pope.
itens.corpo:
The office of camerlengo goes back to the late eleventh century, when Pope Gregory VII suppressed the ancient Roman archdeaconate and transferred its functions of patrimonial administration to a prelate who came to be called «camerarius» — the «chamberlain» in charge of the Apostolic Camera, the central financial curia of the papacy. Throughout the Middle Ages, the office gained extraordinary weight: during the very long vacancy between 1268 and 1271, which lasted almost three years before the election of Gregory X, the cardinals themselves came to be concerned with providing an immediate replacement in case the serving camerlengo died, so great was his importance for the continuity of the Church's administration. In the following centuries, at the head of the Apostolic Camera, the camerlengo accumulated judicial and administrative powers over papal finances, and before the eighteenth century he came to receive annual revenues on the order of ten to twelve thousand scudi — equivalent, in the Papal States, to those of a true minister of Finance, Public Works, and Commerce.

This power entered a marked decline from the nineteenth century onward, first with the administrative reorganizations carried out by Popes Pius VII and Pius IX, and then, definitively, with the loss of the Papal States in 1870. Today the Apostolic Camera retains mainly a ceremonial and transitional function: it falls to the camerlengo of the Holy Roman Church, at the moment of the pope's death or resignation, to administer the temporal goods and rights of the Apostolic See throughout the entire period of vacancy — without, however, holding any power of governance over the universal Church, an exclusive prerogative of the pope and, between elections, of the College of Cardinals itself gathered in conclave. It is the camerlengo who, traditionally, officially ascertains and certifies the death of the pontiff and seals his private apartments, besides requesting from all the offices of the Roman Curia reports on their financial situation and on pending matters; he also receives copies of the current and projected budget of the Holy See and other economic information useful to the cardinals and the future pope, and, together with the dean of the College of Cardinals, plays a central role in organizing the general congregations preparatory to the conclave.

One of the best-known rites associated with the office is the cancellation of the Fisherman's Ring — the personal seal of each pope, used since the thirteenth century to authenticate documents — in the presence of cardinal witnesses: the practice of physically destroying it, to prevent impostors from using false seals on documents, goes back, according to tradition, to 1521 and was maintained until 2013, long after the papal seals had been functionally replaced by a stamp in the mid-nineteenth century. With the resignation of Benedict XVI in 2013, the practice was changed to a deep cross-shaped cut engraved on the seal with a chisel, enough to invalidate it without physically destroying it; the same procedure applies to the lead seal (the «bulla») used to seal papal documents.

The camerlengo's powers are deliberately limited: canon law — today systematized mainly by the apostolic constitution «Universi Dominici Gregis» of 1996 — is explicit in withholding from him any power of governance proper to the pope: he cannot appoint bishops, publish documents of the magisterium, unite or divide dioceses, or make any decision that goes beyond ordinary administration and the material preparation of the conclave. Contrary to what happened in past centuries, when the camerlengo came to hold almost sovereign powers during the vacancy, «Universi Dominici Gregis» itself formally transferred to the College of Cardinals gathered together — and not to a single official — authority over the ordinary affairs of the Apostolic See while the throne of Peter remains vacant. Assisted by three cardinal assistants chosen by lot periodically from among the cardinal electors present in Rome, the camerlengo remains in his functions only until the election of the new pope, when his extraordinary mandate automatically ceases — being, together with the major penitentiary cardinal, one of only two offices of the Roman Curia whose functions do not cease with the vacancy of the See.

On at least one notable occasion, the serving camerlengo himself was elected pope: in 1939, Eugenio Pacelli, who simultaneously held the offices of camerlengo, since April 1, 1935, and Secretary of State, was elected on March 2, 1939 — the day of his 63rd birthday — in the shortest conclave of the twentieth century, held on March 1 and 2 of that year, with only three ballots, becoming Pius XII; he was the first camerlengo to ascend directly to the papacy since Leo XIII, in 1878. In recent decades, the office has been held by the French Cardinal Jean-Louis Tauran, and then by the Irish-American Cardinal Kevin Joseph Farrell — born in Dublin on September 2, 1947, Prefect of the Dicastery for Laity, Family and Life since 2016 —, appointed camerlengo by Francis and installed on February 14, 2019. It was Farrell who exercised these functions during the Sede Vacante opened by the death of Pope Francis on April 21, 2025, acting then as de facto regent of the Holy See — including removing the Fisherman's Ring from Francis's finger —, until the election of Pope Leo XIV on May 8, 2025.

itens.resumo: English Anglican priest who converted to Catholicism, theologian and cardinal-deacon created by Leo XIII in 1879, canonized by Francis in 2019 and proclaimed a Doctor of the Church.
itens.corpo:
John Henry Newman was born in London on February 21, 1801, and died in Edgbaston on August 11, 1890. Educated at Oxford, he was one of the leaders of the Oxford Movement within the Church of England, before his conversion to Catholicism in 1845. He became a Catholic priest and, in 1847, joined the Oratory of Saint Philip Neri, later founding the Birmingham Oratory.

On May 12, 1879, Pope Leo XIII created him a cardinal in consistory, assigning him the diaconia of San Giorgio in Velabro. Newman received the news with surprise, since he had never held a governing post in the Curia, and replied in the famous "Biglietto Speech," in which he argued that one of the Pope's reasons was to please English Catholics and reaffirmed his opposition to what he called the "spirit of liberalism in religion."

His most influential work, the "Essay on the Development of Christian Doctrine" (1845), put forward the thesis that Christian doctrine develops throughout history without losing its identity, an idea that marked later Catholic theology. He also wrote the "Grammar of Assent" (1870), on the nature of the act of faith, and "The Idea of a University," the fruit of his experience as rector.

He was beatified by Benedict XVI on September 19, 2010, and canonized by Francis on October 13, 2019. In 2025, Leo XIV confirmed the opinion of the plenary session of the Dicastery for the Causes of Saints and proclaimed Newman a Doctor of the Church, also declaring him co-patron of the Church's educational mission alongside Saint Thomas Aquinas. He chose as his motto the phrase "Cor ad cor loquitur" ("heart speaks to heart").

itens.resumo: Italian cardinal and hyperpolyglot, celebrated for mastering dozens of languages; created Cardinal Priest of Sant'Onofrio al Gianicolo by Gregory XVI in 1838.
itens.corpo:
Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti was born in Bologna on September 19, 1774, the son of a poor carpenter, and died in Rome on March 15, 1849. He studied with the Piarist fathers and completed his theological studies before the minimum required age, and was ordained a priest. While still very young he was appointed professor of Arabic at the University of Bologna, where he also served as librarian and professor of Oriental languages.

His fame is due to his exceptional linguistic ability: he is estimated to have spoken between 38 and 50 languages fluently, besides reading or understanding many others, such as Quechua and Cornish. The testimony of illustrious contemporaries, among them Lord Byron, helped make him famous throughout Europe; travelers and diplomats sought him out in Rome to test his knowledge with rare dialects and distant languages.

In 1831 he moved to Rome, becoming curator (custos) of the Vatican Library. On February 12, 1838, Pope Gregory XVI created him a cardinal, with the title of Cardinal Priest of Sant'Onofrio al Gianicolo, received on February 15 of that year. He was also a member of the congregations of Propaganda Fide and of other Roman dicasteries.

The first major biography of him, "The Life of Cardinal Mezzofanti" (1858), was written by the cleric Charles William Russell and remains a fundamental source. His last words, according to the tradition recorded by his biographers, were reportedly in Italian: "Andiamo, andiamo, presto in Paradiso!" ("Let us go, let us go, quickly to Paradise!").

itens.resumo: Major Archbishop of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church, imprisoned and sentenced to the Gulag for 18 years, created a cardinal by Paul VI in 1965.
itens.corpo:
Josyf Slipyj was born in Zazdrist, in the Ternopil region, on February 17, 1892, and died in Rome on September 7, 1984. He was one of the main leaders of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church: he became the first rector of the Theological Academy of Lviv and, in 1944, succeeded Metropolitan Andrey Sheptytsky at the head of the Church.

Under the Soviet occupation, he refused to join the official Russian Orthodox Church. In 1945 he was arrested and, after a year of investigation, was sentenced by a military tribunal on charges of "treason against the homeland" (articles 54-1 and 54-11 of the Criminal Code of the Ukrainian SSR) to eight years of forced labor in Gulag camps. In all, he spent 18 years in Soviet prisons, camps and exile. During this period, between 1953 and 1958, he wrote in exile in Maklakovo a multi-volume work on the history of the universal Church in Ukraine.

In 1963, thanks to the intercession of John XXIII and of the American president John F. Kennedy, he was released and was able to leave the Soviet Union. That same year, on December 23, he received the title of Major Archbishop, approved by Paul VI. He was named a cardinal on January 25, 1965, with the title of Cardinal-Priest of Sant'Atanasio, and was solemnly created at the consistory of February 22, 1965. According to the tradition of his Church, he had already been secretly named a cardinal as early as 1949, which only became public later.

In his Roman exile, Slipyj became a spokesman for the religious persecution in the Soviet bloc, but he criticized the Vatican's "Ostpolitik," which he considered excessively lenient toward the Russian Orthodox Church. He persistently advocated the creation of a Ukrainian patriarchate with himself at its head, which was granted neither by Paul VI nor by John Paul II. He founded a Ukrainian seminary, built the Church of Saint Sophia in Rome and the Ukrainian Catholic University. At his death, he was publicly honored by heads of state, as recorded in the official statement of American President Ronald Reagan.

itens.titulo: The Dean of the College of Cardinals
itens.resumo: Office of president of the College of Cardinals, always held by a cardinal bishop and tied to the title of the suburbicarian See of Ostia; first among the cardinals.
itens.corpo:
The Dean of the College of Cardinals is the president of the College of Cardinals and, for this reason, is usually called "first among equals" (primus inter pares) within the Sacred College. He is always a cardinal of the order of bishops and holds, as a sign of his position, the title of the suburbicarian See of Ostia, the most important of the suburban dioceses of Rome, in addition to the title he already held. As a symbol of this condition, he receives the pallium from the hands of the Pope, a vestment normally reserved for metropolitan archbishops.

According to the historical notes of the Annuario Pontificio, the College of Cardinals was constituted in its present form in the year 1150, when it came to have a Dean, who is the bishop of Ostia, and a Camerlengo, administrator of goods during the vacancy of the See of Peter. The precedence of the cardinal bishops over the other members of the ecclesiastical hierarchy was recognized in the ecumenical councils from the Middle Ages onward, with the cardinal bishop of Ostia at the head.

It was at the time of the Council of Trent that Pope Paul IV formalized, by the bull "Cum Venerabiles" of August 22, 1555, the practice that the cardinal bishop of Ostia would also be the Dean of the College. Since 1914, by decree of Pius X, the Dean retains the title of his previous suburbicarian diocese and adds to it that of Ostia; before that, the deans relinquished their previous title in favor of the joint title of Ostia and Velletri.

The Code of Canon Law (canon 352) provides that the Dean is elected by the cardinals who hold a suburbicarian title, under the presidency of the vice-dean, and that his name is presented to the Roman Pontiff, who is to approve the one elected. By decision of Paul VI, in the motu proprio "Sacro Cardinalium Consilio" (February 26, 1965), the cardinals came to elect the Dean from among the cardinal bishops who hold suburbicarian offices, and he receives the title of Cardinal Bishop of Ostia. During the vacancy of the Apostolic See, the Dean plays a central role in conducting the general congregations of the College and presides, among other rites, at the Mass "pro eligendo Romano Pontifice". Among recent deans is the Italian Cardinal Giovanni Battista Re.

itens.resumo: Spanish cardinal (1865–1930), Secretary of State under Saint Pius X and one of the central figures in the struggle against Modernism, created a cardinal at the age of 38 in the consistory of 1903.
itens.corpo:
Rafael Merry del Val y Zulueta was born in London, at the Spanish embassy, on October 10, 1865, the son of the Spanish diplomat and marquis Rafael Merry del Val and Josefina de Zulueta; of Anglo-Spanish descent, he received the full baptismal name Rafael María José Pedro Francisco de Borja Domingo Gerardo de la Santísima Trinidad. He had a remarkably rapid curial career: he was a secret chamberlain at 21, apostolic delegate to Canada at 31 and, at 34, president of the Pontifical Ecclesiastical Academy (Academy of Noble Ecclesiastics) and titular archbishop of Nicaea. While still a deacon, he served as secretary of the conclave of 1903 that elected Giuseppe Sarto as Pius X.

Just a few months later, in the consistory of November 9, 1903, Pius X created him cardinal priest with the title of Santa Prassede, and he received the biretta on November 12. On the same day he was appointed Secretary of State, prefect of the Congregation of Loreto and prefect of the Apostolic Palace — a post he held until August 20, 1914, the eve of the pope's death. His episcopal motto was "Da mihi animas cetera tolle" ("Give me souls, take away the rest").

As Secretary of State and, from 1914, Secretary of the Congregation of the Holy Office (under Benedict XV and Pius XI, who then reserved the prefecture of the dicastery to themselves), Merry del Val was one of the main executors of the repression of Modernism. He was linked to the decree Lamentabili and the encyclical Pascendi Dominici gregis (both from 1907) and to the imposition of the Anti-Modernist Oath of 1910. Although he kept his distance from the more extreme activities of the integralist network Sodalitium Pianum, led by Umberto Benigni — which in 1911 separated from the structure of the Secretariat of State —, his conservative line marked the ecclesiastical policy of the time; it was also he who explained to Theodor Herzl, on behalf of the Holy See, the policy of "non possumus" regarding the nascent Zionist movement.

He took part in the conclave of 1914, which elected Benedict XV. He was also archpriest of the Basilica of Saint Peter and prefect of the Fabric of Saint Peter (1914) and camerlengo of the College of Cardinals between 1911 and 1912. He died in Rome on February 26, 1930. His cause for beatification was introduced with the Congregation of Rites in 1953.

itens.titulo: Jus exclusivae (the veto of the crowns)
itens.resumo: The 'right of exclusion' claimed by Catholic monarchs to veto a candidate for the papacy during the conclave, exercised for the last time in 1903 against Cardinal Rampolla and abolished by Pius X in 1904.
itens.corpo:
The jus exclusivae (Latin for "right of exclusion"), sometimes called the papal veto, was the prerogative that several Catholic monarchs of Europe claimed to exclude a candidate from the papal election. It was never formally recognized by the Church: the kings of France and Spain and the Austrian Empire simply made known to a trusted cardinal — the so-called crown-cardinal — that they considered a given candidate unacceptable. The practice only took clear shape from the mid-seventeenth century onward; in 1644, Spain invoked it to block Cardinal Giulio Cesare Sacchetti, and France attempted a similar maneuver in the same conclave.

The mechanics had a delicate point of timing. The veto was only to be pronounced when the unwanted candidate was close to the two-thirds needed for election — after the election, it would be useless. Since several names could be objectionable to the sovereign, the cardinal in charge sought to delay as long as possible the use of the single veto at his disposal. It did not always work: in the conclave of 1846, the Austrian chancellor Metternich entrusted the veto against Cardinal Mastai-Ferretti to the Archbishop of Milan, Carlo Gaetano Gaisruck, who arrived too late — once elected pope, Mastai-Ferretti would reign for more than thirty-one years as Pius IX. Other uses included the French veto against Cardinal Cavalchini (1758) and the Austrian veto against Cardinal Severoli (1830).

The most famous case was that of 1903, the last in history. Cardinal Mariano Rampolla, Secretary of State of Leo XIII, was the favorite and had gathered a strong majority, but Emperor Franz Joseph I of Austria resolved to exercise the jus exclusivae for political reasons connected with Rampolla's diplomatic alignment, favorable to a rapprochement with France. The one charged with pronouncing the veto was Cardinal Jan Puzyna de Kosielsko, Bishop of Kraków, created a cardinal by Leo XIII on April 15, 1901. The secretary of the conclave, Rafael Merry del Val, later recorded that Puzyna sought him out demanding to announce the veto in the emperor's name, and that he refused even to accept the document; another version indicates that the veto was presented to the Cardinal Camerlengo Oreglia and then communicated to Rampolla himself. According to Puzyna's note, then unpublished, published by L'Osservatore Romano in 2014, after the protest the voting continued: 29 votes for Rampolla, 9 for Gotti and 21 for Cardinal Giuseppe Sarto. Rampolla withdrew from the contest and the conclave elected Sarto, who took the name Pius X.

Already as pope, Pius X abolished the right by the apostolic constitution Commissum Nobis, of January 20, 1904. The text forbade not only the claiming of the veto, but even the mere expression of "a mere wish" to that effect, imposed automatic excommunication (latae sententiae) on anyone who intervened in a future conclave, and obliged the participants to swear that they would tolerate no influence whatsoever from "lay powers of any degree or order." Thus ended, definitively, centuries of interference by the crowns in the election of popes.
